question: Why do we need living prophets today?

quotes.quote: What a blessing it is to live in a time when apostles and prophets are on the earth
whether by mine own voice or by the voice of my servants

answer:
We need living prophets because **Jesus Christ still leads His Church and still reveals His will today**. Scriptures and teachings from past prophets are essential, but living prophets help us apply eternal principles to the circumstances and challenges of our own time.

In October 2026 General Conference, Elder Vaiangina Sikahema taught that “What a blessing it is to live in a time when apostles and prophets are on the earth” (“Prophets, Seers, and Revelators”). He explained that people in many periods of history longed for prophetic guidance, and he warned us not to treat God’s revealed word lightly. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/15sikahema?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))

Living prophets bless us by:

- **Testifying of Jesus Christ** and teaching His restored gospel.
- **Receiving revelation** to guide the Church.
- **Warning and correcting us** when worldly ideas pull us away from God.
- **Helping us apply the gospel** to present conditions.
- **Providing unified direction** for the worldwide Church.

Elder Sikahema also referred to the Lord’s declaration that His word comes “whether by mine own voice or by the voice of my servants” (“Prophets, Seers, and Revelators”). Thus, listening to a living prophet is not replacing the Savior or the scriptures; it is one way the Savior speaks to His children now. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/15sikahema?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))

We should prayerfully study prophetic counsel, seek confirmation through the Holy Ghost, and then act in faith. General Conference teaches that prophetic counsel can become a means of receiving personal revelation from the Lord. ([newsroom.churchofjesuschrist.org](https://newsroom.churchofjesuschrist.org/event/october-2026-general-conference?utm_source=openai))

question: How can the Holy Ghost comfort me when I'm grieving?

quotes.quote: The Savior’s peace is made manifest through the comforting power of the Holy Ghost.
I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.

answer:
The Holy Ghost can comfort you by helping you feel the Savior’s presence when your loss cannot be fixed. In his October 2026 general conference talk **“Comfort from the Holy Ghost,” Elder Matthew J. Eyring** taught that as we humbly turn to Jesus Christ and cast our burdens on Him, the Lord provides comfort and answers in His own time. Those answers may come through spiritual impressions, helpful people, resources, or priesthood blessings. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/29eyring?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))

You might experience that comfort as:

- **Peace amid intense sorrow.** Elder Eyring said, “The Savior’s peace is made manifest through the comforting power of the Holy Ghost.” This peace may not remove your grief immediately, but it can help you endure one moment or one day at a time. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/29eyring?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))
- **Hope in Jesus Christ.** The Holy Ghost testifies that death is not the end and that the Savior’s Resurrection gives eternal perspective. Elder Eyring taught that this belief can give us courage when loved ones die—even when the death feels premature. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/29eyring?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))
- **Assurance that you are not abandoned.** Elder Eyring ended by quoting the Savior’s promise, “I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.” ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/29eyring?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))
- **Strength to receive help.** Pray honestly, attend the temple or sacrament meeting as you are able, ask for a priesthood blessing, and let trusted people mourn with you.

Grieving does not mean your faith is weak. As you keep turning toward Christ, the Holy Ghost can bring quiet reassurance, sustaining peace, and hope that healing and reunion are possible through Him.

question: Why should I pay tithing when money is tight?

quotes.quote: the law of tithing is a law of faith.
in His own time and way.

answer:
Money being tight is precisely when tithing becomes an act of faith—but it should not be viewed as a guarantee that money will suddenly appear or that faithful members will never experience hardship.

In October 2026 General Conference, Elder Patricio M. Giuffra taught in **“Trusting the Lord Through Tithes and Offerings”** that “the law of tithing is a law of faith.” He shared the story of a woman whose income barely covered rent, fuel, and food. Elder Giuffra emphasized that the Lord knows our financial circumstances and fulfills His promises “in His own time and way.” ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/24giuffra?lang=bfi))

Elder Moisés Villanueva likewise spoke in **“Prove Me Now Herewith”** about his family’s poverty and his mother’s decision to pay a full tithe. He explained that the blessings may be “significant but subtle,” including spiritual guidance, gratitude, employment, health, and help managing resources—not merely a higher salary or promotion. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/53villanueva?lang=eng))

So, why pay when money is tight?

- To put God first and show trust in Jesus Christ.
- To keep a covenant commandment even when obedience requires sacrifice.
- To invite spiritual strength, peace, guidance, and the Lord’s help.
- To learn that God’s blessings do not always come in the form we expect.

At the same time, do not face genuine deprivation alone. The Church’s handbook says bishops may use fast offerings to help with essential needs such as food, housing, utilities, and medical care. If you cannot meet basic needs, speak honestly with your bishop or Relief Society president while continuing to seek the Lord’s guidance. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/manual/general-handbook/22-providing-for-temporal-needs?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))

question: What does it mean to be sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise?

quotes.quote: when sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise, an ordinance, vow, or covenant is binding on earth and in heaven.
confirms as acceptable to God the righteous acts, ordinances, and covenants

answer:
To be **sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise** means that the Holy Ghost confirms that an ordinance has been performed properly and that we are faithfully honoring the covenants connected with it. In this role, the Holy Ghost ratifies or approves our righteous choices before God.

In his October 2026 General Conference talk **“Sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise,” Elder David A. Bednar** taught that “when sealed by the Holy Spirit of Promise, an ordinance, vow, or covenant is binding on earth and in heaven.” ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/54bednar?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))

This sealing is not merely automatic because we have received a baptism, temple endowment, or temple sealing. Elder Bednar explained that the ratifying seal generally comes **“over time”** as we sincerely repent, honor our covenants, and yield our hearts to God. It is conditional: unrighteousness can cause a person to forfeit the promised blessings. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/54bednar?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))

The Church’s *Guide to the Scriptures* similarly teaches that the Holy Ghost “confirms as acceptable to God the righteous acts, ordinances, and covenants” of His children. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/scriptures/gs/holy-spirit-of-promise?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))

In simple terms:

- **The ordinance** is performed by priesthood authority.
- **The covenant** involves promises between us and God.
- **The Holy Ghost** witnesses whether we are faithfully living those promises.
- **The sealing** makes the covenant spiritually valid and binding beyond this life.

This doctrine is ultimately hopeful, not merely cautionary. Through the Atonement of Jesus Christ, repentance, and continued faithfulness, we can receive the Holy Ghost’s confirming witness and the blessings God has promised.

question: What did President Oaks say in his closing remarks?

quotes.quote: concentrate our worship, focus our learning, and unite our testimonies
Unto him that receiveth I will give more.

answer:
In his **“Closing Remarks”** at the October 2026 General Conference, President Dallin H. Oaks said that the conference messages and Spirit of the Lord should help us **“concentrate our worship, focus our learning, and unite our testimonies”** on Jesus Christ and Heavenly Father’s plan. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/510oaks?lang=asf&utm_source=openai))

He invited everyone to study and ponder the conference talks prayerfully and then act in faith on their teachings, reminding us of the Lord’s promise: **“Unto him that receiveth I will give more.”** ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/510oaks?lang=asf&utm_source=openai))

President Oaks also announced the upcoming **Salt Lake Temple Celebration**. He said the temple doors will open to the public on **April 5, 2027**, the first such opening since 1893. He also mentioned the premiere of the new video series *Dedicate*, including a future virtual tour of the temple. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/510oaks?lang=asf&utm_source=openai))

He concluded by blessing Church members and their families with peace and contentment and by testifying that the restored gospel of Jesus Christ is found in His Church. He said that truth—including truth about the covenant path—will lead us to the destiny Heavenly Father desires for us. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/510oaks?lang=asf&utm_source=openai))

question: How should I talk to people I strongly disagree with?

quotes.quote: strengthen confidence and preserve relationships.
I respect your view,
Let us slow down and talk,
I don’t want this to divide us.
truth and love always walk together.

answer:
October 2026 General Conference gave clear counsel on this.

**First, slow down and listen.** Elder Clark G. Gilbert, in “Teach Truth with Love,” described how resisting the impulse to respond helped him understand people’s struggles and find common ground. He taught that we should not assume hostility is the whole story; a person may be carrying pain or regret we cannot see. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/59gilbert?lang=eng))

**Second, choose peaceful language.** Elder Alfred Kyungu, in “Using the Language of Peacemakers,” counseled us to use words that “strengthen confidence and preserve relationships.” He suggested phrases such as “I respect your view,” “Let us slow down and talk,” and “I don’t want this to divide us.” ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/47kyungu?lang=eng))

**Third, do not confuse love with surrendering truth.** Elder Gilbert taught that “truth and love always walk together.” We can state what we believe firmly while avoiding anger, ridicule, or personal attacks. Sometimes the most Christlike response is to postpone the conversation—or remain respectfully silent—when the setting has become too contentious. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/59gilbert?lang=eng))

**Finally, keep Jesus Christ at the center.** President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, in “Christ-Centered Unity,” taught that as we become more patient, kind, forgiving, and helpful, there is less room for pride, judgment, and contention. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/51uchtdorf?lang=eng))

A practical pattern might be: **listen first, acknowledge the person’s dignity, explain your view calmly, avoid trying to “win,” and end the conversation if it becomes unproductive.** Pray to see the person as a child of God—not merely as someone who holds an opposing opinion.

question: How can our ward be united when members are so different from each other?

quotes.quote: The closer we come to Him, the closer we will come to each other.
I respect your view,
We can work this out,
I don’t want this to divide us.

answer:
Yes—the October 2026 General Conference addressed this directly, especially President Dieter F. Uchtdorf’s talk **“Christ-Centered Unity.”**

A ward does not become united by making everyone alike. It becomes united by helping everyone turn toward the same Savior. President Uchtdorf taught, “The closer we come to Him, the closer we will come to each other.” He also explained that our unity is not based on political views, culture, or personal interests, but on love for God and neighbor and commitment to Jesus Christ and His gospel. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/51uchtdorf?lang=asf&utm_source=openai))

That suggests several practical steps for your ward:

1. **Center meetings and activities on Christ.** The sacrament is a weekly reminder that we are not alone—we have the Savior and one another. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/51uchtdorf?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))  
2. **See individuals rather than labels.** President Rosemary K. Chibota, in **“A Child of God,”** urged us to see others as the Savior sees them. Her memorable expression was “I see you”—a simple way to communicate that someone matters. Learn names, listen to experiences, and notice those who may feel overlooked. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/42chibota?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))  
3. **Speak as peacemakers.** In **“Using the Language of Peacemakers,”** Elder Alfred Kyungu encouraged words such as “I respect your view,” “We can work this out,” and “I don’t want this to divide us.” ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/47kyungu?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))  
4. **Serve across differences.** Shared ministering, compassionate service, and ward responsibilities can help members discover spiritual common ground.

Unity is not sameness. It is choosing love, patience, humility, and covenant discipleship while appreciating the different gifts each member brings. Every small effort to build a bridge rather than a wall contributes to Christ-centered unity.

question: What did Elder Christofferson teach about wisdom?

quotes.quote: Where will this lead?
not only to refrain from gambling but to use the time and resources saved thereby for doing good.
anxiously engaged in a good cause
bring to pass much righteousness.

answer:
In his October 2026 General Conference talk **“O Be Wise,” President D. Todd Christofferson** taught that wisdom means recognizing the spiritual and practical costs of gambling and choosing to use our agency, time, and resources for worthwhile purposes.

He explained that gambling is not merely a harmless pastime. It is built on gaining something at another person’s expense, which conflicts with the commandment to love our neighbors. He also warned that gambling can displace saving, relationships, work, and other worthwhile pursuits.

President Christofferson emphasized the principle of **opportunity cost**—that choosing one activity means giving up opportunities to do something else. Quoting President Dallin H. Oaks, he asked, **“Where will this lead?”** and encouraged us to consider the future effects of present choices. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/19christofferson?lang=eng))

His central plea was: **“not only to refrain from gambling but to use the time and resources saved thereby for doing good.”** He connected wise living with being productive, supporting honest work, and contributing to the well-being of others rather than pursuing idle or selfish gain. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/19christofferson?lang=eng))

He concluded by directing us toward the Lord’s counsel to be **“anxiously engaged in a good cause”** and to **“bring to pass much righteousness.”** Thus, wisdom is not simply avoiding harmful behavior; it is actively choosing pursuits that build faith, bless families, serve others, and lead us toward righteousness. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/19christofferson?lang=eng))

question: Is the gospel only for certain kinds of people?

quotes.quote: inviteth all to come unto him
denieth none that come unto him.
His grace is for all.
We are all a work in progress.
relentless in His loving pursuit of each of you.
What is one step toward Jesus Christ that I can take today?

answer:
No. **The gospel of Jesus Christ is for every person**, regardless of background, culture, past mistakes, doubts, abilities, or present spiritual strength.

In his October 2026 General Conference talk **“The Gospel of Jesus Christ Is for All,” President Dallin H. Oaks** taught that the Savior’s invitation is universal. Quoting the Book of Mormon, he emphasized that Christ “inviteth all to come unto him” and “denieth none that come unto him.” President Oaks then stated plainly: **“His grace is for all.”** ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/49oaks?id=p_gOuXv&lang=eng&utm_source=openai))

That does not mean the gospel asks nothing of us. Faith, repentance, covenants, and following Christ matter. But those invitations and requirements are extended to everyone—not only to people who already feel worthy, confident, or spiritually strong. President Oaks reminded us, **“We are all a work in progress.”** He also taught that the Lord is “relentless in His loving pursuit of each of you.” ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/49oaks?id=p_gOuXv&lang=eng&utm_source=openai))

So the gospel is not reserved for a particular “kind” of person. It is precisely for people who need healing, forgiveness, direction, belonging, and hope—which is all of us. The Church’s October 2026 conference summaries likewise describe the message as an invitation for all people to come unto Christ. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10?lang=bfi&utm_source=openai))

A helpful question may be: **“What is one step toward Jesus Christ that I can take today?”** The answer need not be perfect or dramatic. The Savior invites you to come as you are and let Him help you become more like Him.

question: What does the Church teach about using artificial intelligence?

quotes.quote: Artificial intelligence cannot replace revelation or generate truth from God

answer:
The **October 2026 General Conference did not give a specific message about artificial intelligence**. The Church’s clearest current guidance comes from the *General Handbook* and recent teachings by Church leaders.

The Church does **not** teach that AI is inherently evil. It may be used as a tool for learning, research, editing, translation, communication, and service. But it must support—not replace—our relationship with God, personal revelation, moral agency, human effort, and genuine relationships.

Key principles include:

- **Rely on revelation and the Holy Ghost.** AI cannot provide revelation or determine truth from God. Elder Gerrit W. Gong taught, “Artificial intelligence cannot replace revelation or generate truth from God” in his 2026 workshop *Faith, Dignity, and Human Flourishing: Hearing God’s Voice in an Age of Artificial Intelligence*. ([newsroom.churchofjesuschrist.org](https://newsroom.churchofjesuschrist.org/article/transcript-faith-dignity-and-human-flourishing-hearing-god-s-voice-in-an-age-of-artificial-intelligence?utm_source=openai))
- **Use it honestly and responsibly.** Members should not use AI to create or spread false, misleading, illegal, or harmful material. AI-generated information should be checked for accuracy. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/manual/general-handbook/38-church-policies-and-guidelines?id=title104-p319&lang=eng&title104=&utm_source=openai))
- **Do your own spiritual and intellectual work.** AI should not write talks, lessons, prayers, or blessings in place of personal preparation and inspiration. It may assist with research, editing, and translation, but it should not replace effort or testimony. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/manual/general-handbook/38-church-policies-and-guidelines?id=title104-p319&lang=eng&title104=&utm_source=openai))
- **Protect privacy and relationships.** Do not enter confidential Church or personal information into unapproved AI tools, and do not depend on AI for companionship, emotional support, or life guidance. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/manual/general-handbook/38-church-policies-and-guidelines?id=title104-p319&lang=eng&title104=&utm_source=openai))

In short, Latter-day Saints can use AI as a helpful servant, but should never allow it to become a substitute for God, the Holy Ghost, prophets, scripture, personal effort, or loving human relationships.

question: What did the conference teach about foreordination?

quotes.quote: God held you in reserve for this time.
You were taught and prepared, before you were born, to invite God’s children to come unto Christ.

answer:
The October 2026 General Conference did **not** include a talk specifically titled or indexed under *foreordination*. However, Bishop Sean Douglas taught a closely related principle in **“The Hour of Your Mission Is Come.”**

He taught that God prepared His children before mortality for important work in this dispensation:

> “God held you in reserve for this time.”

He also said:

> “You were taught and prepared, before you were born, to invite God’s children to come unto Christ.”

This reflects the doctrine that, in the premortal world, God appointed His children to certain responsibilities. It also emphasizes that our foreordained purposes are connected to gathering Israel and sharing the gospel—not to personal status or guaranteed outcomes. We still must exercise agency, accept opportunities, and faithfully serve.

The message was especially directed to the rising generation and missionary service. Bishop Douglas urged young people not to become distracted from their responsibility to help others come unto Christ, reminding them: “You are needed!” ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/general-conference/2026/10/18douglas?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))

So, in summary, conference taught that:

- God knew and prepared us before we were born.
- We may have been prepared for significant responsibilities in this latter-day work.
- Missionary service and inviting others to Christ can be part of that divine preparation.
- Foreordination should lead to faithful action, not complacency.

The broader Church explanation remains important: foreordination does **not** guarantee a particular calling or outcome; opportunities are received in mortality as we exercise agency and remain worthy. ([churchofjesuschrist.org](https://www.churchofjesuschrist.org/study/manual/gospel-topics/foreordination?lang=eng&utm_source=openai))
